name: material_plane_press_slide
description: An oversized finite plane is pressed onto the whole nominal sensor footprint under a commanded 5 N load, held, slid 2 mm at 5 mm/s with the load maintained, and held again. The slide is integrated with mass. All recorded states must keep macroscopic contact over the imaged region.

config_contract.composition: Simulation inputs select object geometry, material case and parameter overrides, surface, and contact; this setup supplies shared sensor, fixture, protocol, and numerics.
config_contract.current_loader_behavior: Shared setup only; run a contact_simulation config with run --config. The object geometry selects the mechanical adapter.
config_contract.sensor_baseline: The current checkout uses a uniform gel; these configs preserve that baseline and do not restore a separate coating.
config_contract.parameter_policy: Values are illustrative starting points; numerical validity and real-sensor calibration are separate requirements.

notes: A finite-thickness layer is required for deformable material behavior; plane describes the nominal contacting face.
The plane must cover the deformed sensor footprint throughout the full x travel.

protocol.travel_meaning: An outcome, not a command: the coupled platen is free in z under a commanded normal load, and its position is read back per substep and recorded as platen_travel_m.

initialization.note: A load cannot close an open gap, so contact is established by travel and the platen is then handed over to load control. The preload has to stay below the target on the stiffest specimen in the comparison: the rigid reference reaches 5 N at 0.092 mm, so 0.030 mm leaves margin, and the softer materials simply start further from the target and are pressed to it. This is the one travel that is still a command.

notes: Every case in this comparison is pressed to the same 5 N, which is the measured load of the experiment it represents.

Equal travel is not equal load. A rigid specimen leaves the gel carrying everything while foam absorbs most of it, so a travel-driven comparison compares materials at different loads, and each preset has to be refitted to its own material. Commanding the load removes both problems: one protocol transfers to every specimen, and the travel each one needs becomes a measurement rather than a setting.
The press ramps from 1 N so the handover from preload to load control is gradual whichever side of 1 N the preload landed on.

The slide accelerates into its 5 mm/s over 0.2 s (500 um) instead of stepping into it: a velocity step is an infinite acceleration once mass is present, and even quasi-statically it asked every contact point to cross its elastic slip allowance in a single increment.

The slide is integrated with mass at 0.1 ms; see protocol.transient. It is the expensive part of the protocol, and it sets the slide distance: the completed rigid reference converged about 16,800 substeps per second of sliding, so every additional millimetre costs about 3,400 substeps of transient solving. 2 mm is what the rigid reference showed is needed - it reaches steady sliding, its first stick-slip release, and re-stick in the hold - rather than what a longer traverse would add.

The holds are 0.3 s. The rigid reference re-sticks within 0.1 s of the platen stopping, so 0.3 s covers it. For the viscoelastic specimens neither hold reaches equilibrium: their slow Prony branch is 2 s, so the slide starts and the record ends while the material is still creeping. That is a property of the protocol, identical for every specimen, not a settling time to read a relaxed modulus from.

windows.reason: The whole slide is integrated with mass. A quasi-static solve loses the slide at its onset: contact points around the gel's free rim leave stick and then open, each release dumping stored elastic energy in one instant, and Newton's trial step turns a gel element inside out. With mass the release is an acceleration and the solve carries on, at two iterations a substep. Inertia is switched on 10 ms before the slide, inside the hold, so the transition and the first contact event are not the same load step.

transient.note: Physical damping comes from the specimen's Prony branches. TINTP amplitude decay removes only the integrator's own high-frequency content; no Rayleigh terms are added on top of the material law.

macroscopic_contact_bins.region_note: A slide unloads the gel's free corners while the imaged region stays well seated, and those corners lie outside every frame the dataset holds. Geometric footprint coverage, edge margin and total repulsive force stay gated on the whole outer surface, and active_bin_fraction for that whole surface is recorded in every frame. See docs/convergence.md.

contact_acceptance.initial_state_adjustment: No silent preload increase or contact constraint change; revise the config if preload does not achieve acceptance.

discretization.note: The default gel uses sensor.gel.elements (36 x 30 x 8). Set gel_mesh to refined to opt into the 0.125 mm whole-surface grid and graded depth. Object mesh resolution is independent. Fine texture accuracy requires a refinement comparison.

object_mesh.rigid_texture_note: Half the gel's 0.70 x 0.69 mm contact face, so the target is finer than the surface that has to sense it without being finer than anything that surface can register. It also has to satisfy the case's own minimum_elements_per_shortest_wavelength, which validation checks against both this size and the gel mesh. It used to be built at common_contact_surface_max_edge_m instead: 0.125 mm, 48 quads across the shortest wavelength where the case asked for 8, and 134,400 target segments for a shape the gel samples 1,080 times.
object_mesh.note: Object discretization is independent of the unchanged gel mesh. Use matched to compare against the original contact-matched solid grid.

contact_numerics.pinball_note: Absolute pinball radius. Points farther than this from the target are not searched; 4 mm is well beyond any gap the protocol opens and far below the footprint, so it neither misses contact nor slows the search.
contact_numerics.penetration_note: Penetration scales as 1/FKN. At FKN = 1 it was measured at 26.4 um, a sixth of the 150 um of surface deformation the renderer reads, and a penetration tolerance of 1 um below that forces augmentation on nearly every substep: contact status then chatters, and the chattering climbs with sliding distance until the solve stops. FKN = 10 brings penetration to 0.69 um and a 10 um tolerance sits well above it, so augmentation rarely fires. The accuracy and the convergence improve together; this is not a trade.
contact_numerics.tangential_pair_note: FKT and SLTO are raised together, so the elastic slip the interface tolerates - their ratio - is unchanged at 2.5 um and the contact is exactly as stiff. What changes is how often augmented Lagrange revisits a converged state to update its multipliers. At FKT = 1 each revisit threw the residual up by as much as two orders of magnitude, and the slide was lost within tens of micrometres.

solver.note: Large deflection (NLGEOM) is always on. The analysis is quasi-static except inside protocol.transient windows, which integrate mass. GPU acceleration is requested and verified by the run; a formulation the GPU cannot solve stops the run rather than silently changing the model. transient_points_per_cycle and predict_cutback are CUTCONTROL settings; null and true leave ANSYS's own. The 150-iteration ceiling leaves headroom for contact status changes; it used to be imposed silently on top of a declared 80, so a resolved run disagreed with the setup it came from. cores, gpu, require_gpu and allow_unlisted_gpu say where a run executes and are the only solver settings a resolved run may hold differently from this block.

limitations: This sequence has no release, so recovery after separation and adhesive pull-off are not observed.
A single 2 mm x slide cannot identify all anisotropic parameters or all rate dependence, and neither hold is long enough to read an equilibrium modulus from.
The fluffy case represents an effective layer; it does not resolve individual fibers.
The slide is integrated with mass, but no vibration channel is calibrated or claimed.
Platen travel is an outcome here, so a case's indentation depth is a result to read, not a parameter to compare against another run's.
